name: Cabbage aphid
description: Brevicoryne brassicae (L.), the cabbage aphid, on Brassica crops. Weather-rule risk bands derived from the agronomic literature (see _encoding_notes).

rules.name: High pressure — optimal warm, dry conditions
rules.description: Temperature within the 20-25 C population-growth optimum (r_m peaks at 25 C; Soh et al. 2018) with zero recorded precipitation in the hour (see the literature cited below). The literature supports only a qualitative dampening direction for precipitation, not a sourced numeric rate cutoff — so this rule gates on 'no precipitation recorded' (0 mm) rather than an invented magnitude threshold: any recorded precipitation in the hour, however small, downgrades to moderate via the next rule instead.

rules.name: Moderate pressure — optimal temperature band, wet hour
rules.description: Same 20-25 C optimum as the high-pressure rule, but with any recorded precipitation in the hour (> 0 mm). The literature: precipitation is a documented (if regionally contested) dampening factor, so this hour is downgraded rather than counted as high risk; the gate is zero-vs-nonzero, not a rate threshold, because no source in the literature review gives a dose-response magnitude for BRVCBR.

rules.name: Moderate pressure — upper transitional band
rules.description: 25-30 C: nymph-to-adult development time is still short (Soh et al. 2018: ~5.05-5.08 days) but the intrinsic rate of increase is falling toward the population-decline threshold observed at 30 C. Treated as a caution band, not full high pressure.

rules.name: Moderate pressure — lower transitional band
rules.description: 15-20 C: development continues (Soh et al. 2018: ~6.4-10.4 days nymph-to-adult) but below the 20-25 C population-growth optimum.

_encoding_notes: No rule fires below 15 C or above 30 C; calculate_risk_index_probability_wd's per-hour default of 'low' applies there, consistent with the literature's ~4 C lower developmental threshold and its cautious ~30 C+ upper caution bound.

Humidity (atmospheric_relative_humidity) is deliberately NOT used as a hard gate on any rule: the literature found directly conflicting field evidence on the sign of the humidity effect across studies/regions. Encoding an unproven directional humidity gate would overstate the science; this is left for agronomic review rather than guessed.

The precipitation gate (0 mm, i.e. zero-vs-nonzero recorded precipitation in the hour) is deliberately NOT a numeric rate threshold: the literature review gives a sourced qualitative dampening direction but no sourced dose-response magnitude for BRVCBR.
The economic-threshold percentage (10% plants infested per UNH Extension) is a scouting/ground-truth concept, not a weather-rule condition, and is intentionally not encoded here.
